facts.info: William Shakespeare (1564-1616) was an English playwright, poet, and actor, widely regarded as the greatest writer in the English language.

evidence.text: William Shakespeare was an English playwright, poet and actor widely regarded as the greatest writer in the English language and the world's greatest dramatist.

facts.info: Charles Dickens (1812-1870) was an English writer and social critic. Created some of the world's best-known fictional characters.

evidence.text: Charles John Huffam Dickens was an English novelist and social critic who created some of the world's best-known fictional characters.

facts.info: Leo Tolstoy (1828-1910) was a Russian writer regarded as one of the greatest authors of all time.

evidence.text: Count Lev Nikolayevich Tolstoy, usually referred to in English as Leo Tolstoy, was a Russian writer who is regarded as one of the greatest authors of all time.

facts.info: Jane Austen (1775-1817) was an English novelist known for her witty social commentary and realistic portrayal of women's lives.

evidence.text: Jane Austen was an English novelist known primarily for her six major novels, which interpret, critique, and comment upon the British landed gentry at the end of the 18th century.

facts.info: Ernest Hemingway (1899-1961) was an American novelist, short-story writer, and journalist. Known for his economical, understated style.
works: The Old Man and the Sea

evidence.text: Ernest Miller Hemingway was an American novelist, short-story writer and journalist whose economical and understated style strongly influenced 20th-century fiction.

facts.info: George Orwell (1903-1950) was an English novelist, essayist, and critic. Known for his social critique and opposition to totalitarianism.

evidence.text: Eric Arthur Blair, better known by his pen name George Orwell, was an English novelist, essayist, journalist, and critic characterized by lucid prose, biting social criticism, and opposition to totalitarianism.

facts.info: Victor Hugo (1802-1885) was a French poet, novelist, and dramatist of the Romantic movement.

evidence.text: Victor-Marie Hugo was a French Romantic poet, novelist, and dramatist considered one of the greatest and best-known French writers.

facts.info: Fyodor Dostoevsky (1821-1881) was a Russian novelist, philosopher, and essayist. Known for psychological depth and exploration of human nature.

evidence.text: Fyodor Mikhailovich Dostoevsky was a Russian novelist, short story writer, essayist, and journalist whose literary works explore the human condition in the troubled political, social, and spiritual atmospheres of 19th-century Russia.

facts.description: Romanticism was an artistic, literary, musical, and intellectual movement (late 18th to mid-19th century) emphasizing emotion, individualism, and nature as a source of inspiration. Key figures: Wordsworth, Shelley, Hugo, Goethe.

evidence.text: Romanticism was an artistic and intellectual movement that originated in Europe towards the end of the 18th century, emphasizing emotion and individualism.

facts.description: Realism was a 19th-century literary movement that sought to depict everyday life accurately, without romantic idealization. Key figures: Balzac, Flaubert, Tolstoy, Dickens.

evidence.text: Literary realism is part of the realist art movement that sought to represent familiar things as they are, everyday, middle- and lower-class life.

facts.description: Modernism was an early 20th-century movement characterized by a break with traditional forms, experimentation with narrative structure, and focus on inner consciousness. Key figures: Joyce, Woolf, Proust, Kafka.

evidence.text: Modernism in literature emerged in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, mainly in Europe and North America, characterized by a self-conscious break with traditional ways of writing.

facts.description: Gothic literature is a genre combining fiction, horror, death, and romance. Originated in 18th-century England with Horace Walpole's 'The Castle of Otranto'.

evidence.text: Gothic fiction, sometimes called Gothic horror in the 20th century, is a genre of literature and film that covers horror, death, and at times romance.
